doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

chapter: Growing up with his father and Joe Morello
title: How Morello got his start from the Grand Ole Opry to Marian McPartland
summary: Caputo's father got Morello his first job; Morello lost his Springfield job to a returning serviceman and went to New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And he had a start with — well Marian McPartland was kind a of big part of his initial career, wasn’t it?
Yes. They had to — my father got Joe Morello’s his first job in the Grand Ole Opry.
My father got Joe Morello his first job he played, in the Grand Ole Opry.

Yes, which was country music, a little known fact. And you know then people started to listen to this guy, wow, he’s quite a drummer. And then he came home and they literally had to force Joe Morello to go to New York City. He was playing at the Club 21 in Springfield with Whitey Bernard on Hammond organ. And he took the place of Joe Rasch, who was an area drummer. And Joe Rasch went into the service. Well Joe took his job and played with Whitey Bernard. Joe Rasch came back and as was law, you had to give back the job that you left. So Joe Morello had to vacate his position.
That a returning serviceman was entitled to his job if he wanted it.
Exactly. So Joe Rasch wanted his job back and Joe Morello was out and with no job they brought him down to New York City, and Marian McPartland listened to him, and the rest is history.
It was at the Hickory House.
Did the Brubeck thing, didn’t Brubeck hang out down there a little bit and hear him?
